claims: Autumn Durald Arkapaw won Best Cinematography at the 2026 Oscars for the film Sinners.
Autumn Durald Arkapaw is the first woman in Academy Awards history to win the Best Cinematography award.
Autumn Durald Arkapaw is the first woman of color to win Best Cinematography at the Oscars.
The Best Cinematography Oscar category has a 98-year history.
Autumn Durald Arkapaw is the first woman to shoot on the large IMAX 65mm format for a film.
Autumn Durald Arkapaw is the first woman to shoot on the Ultra Panavision format for a film.
Sinners is director Ryan Coogler's 1930s-set vampire film.
The Los Angeles Times stated that Autumn Durald Arkapaw's work on Sinners captured the gritty reality of a Mississippi juke joint.
The Los Angeles Times stated that Autumn Durald Arkapaw's work on Sinners captured surreal, expressionistic scenes.
Sinners by Autumn Durald Arkapaw won the 2026 Best Cinematography Oscar.
Frankenstein by Dan Laustsen was nominated for the 2026 Best Cinematography Oscar.
Marty Supreme by Darius Khondji was nominated for the 2026 Best Cinematography Oscar.
One Battle After Another by Michael Bauman was nominated for the 2026 Best Cinematography Oscar.
Train Dreams by Adolpho Veloso was nominated for the 2026 Best Cinematography Oscar.
Vanity Fair notes that the 2026 Best Cinematography Oscar nominees included Darius Khondji and Dan Laustsen
